--- original
+++ modified
@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: ffe980
+project: swift-validator
+title: 'swift: expand the swiftlint tool rules, and copy Airbnb''s three custom regex rules'
+---
+We already drive real `swiftlint` from four `code-hygiene` rules. We use it for function-length, magic-numbers and missing-docs only. SwiftLint decides six more things our prompt rules currently judge, and Airbnb ships three custom regex rules that convert judgment into a deterministic check.
+
+Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/airbnb/swift/master/Sources/AirbnbSwiftFormatTool/swiftlint.yml
+
+## Stock rules to turn on
+
+| SwiftLint rule | Supersedes (prompt rule) |
+|---|---|
+| `implicitly_unwrapped_optional` | `optionals.md` no IUO |
+| `force_unwrapping` | `optionals.md` no force unwrap in non-test code |
+| `force_try` | `error-handling.md` no `try!` in non-test code |
+| `force_cast` | `error-handling.md` no `as!` in non-test code |
+| `unused_optional_binding` | `optionals.md` check for nil, do not bind an unused value |
+| `unowned_variable_capture` | (new — we have no rule) |
+| `legacy_constructor`, `legacy_nsgeometry_functions`, `legacy_cggeometry_functions` | (new — we have no rule) |
+
+Keep our existing test-code carve-outs. `force_unwrapping`, `force_try` and `force_cast` must stay off inside test targets — our rules say "in non-test code" and mean it. Airbnb solves this with `noForceUnwrapInTests` / `noForceTryInTests`, which apply the opposite polarity in tests. Honour the same split.
+
+## The three custom regex rules — copy these
+
+Each one turns an LLM judgment into a regex plus an escape hatch:
+
+1. `no_direct_standard_out_logs` — bans `print`, `debugPrint`, `dump`, `Swift.print`, `_printChanges`, scoped by `match_kinds: [identifier]`. We have NO rule for this.
+2. `no_file_literal` — bans `#file`, scoped by `match_kinds: [keyword]`. We have NO rule for this.
+3. `no_unchecked_sendable` — bans `@unchecked Sendable`, scoped by `match_kinds: [attribute.builtin, typeidentifier]`.
+
+## The mechanism that matters most
+
+Read Airbnb's `no_unchecked_sendable` message:
+
+> "If you really must use `@unchecked Sendable`, you can add a `// swiftlint:disable:next no_unchecked_sendable` annotation with an explanation for how we know the type is thread-safe…"
+
+The escape hatch IS the documentation. Our `concurrency.md` states the same requirement as pure judgment: "`@unchecked Sendable` requires a documented synchronization invariant. The smell is the *absence* of a lock/isolation mechanism and a comment." A tool cannot judge "is there a documented invariant" — but it CAN require an explicit annotation, and the annotation text is the invariant.
+
+This is the `objectivity-over-judgment` standing order working in production: exemptions become annotations. Write the finding message so it tells the author exactly what to write, as Airbnb's does.
+
+## Acceptance
+
+- Pass and fail fixtures per rule group, in `builtin/validators/code-hygiene/fixtures/`.
+- A shipped acceptance test driving REAL `swiftlint`. Model it on `missing_docs.rs:2049-2165` and `magic_numbers.rs:243-330`.
+- A test proving the annotation escape hatch works: a `@unchecked Sendable` with the disable comment produces NO finding; the same code without it produces one.
+- A test proving the test-target polarity split: a force unwrap in `Sources/` reports; the same in `Tests/` does not.
+- Update the `mirdan` fixture roster at `crates/mirdan/src/builtin_validators.rs`. #tool-validators
\ No newline at end of file

+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m0mz7f6zshwwvym4v8m2dp4z
+  text: |-
+    Research done. Measurements taken with swiftlint 0.65.0 before any edit.
+
+    **Every rule name the card lists is PRESENT in swiftlint 0.65.0.** Checked each of the nine against `swiftlint rules`: `implicitly_unwrapped_optional`, `force_unwrapping`, `force_try`, `force_cast`, `unused_optional_binding`, `unowned_variable_capture`, `legacy_constructor`, `legacy_nsgeometry_functions`, `legacy_cggeometry_functions`. No name has to be dropped.
+
+    **`force_try` and `force_cast` default to `severity: error`.** An error-severity finding makes swiftlint exit 2. The child config states `severity: warning` for every rule, so the run exits 0.
+
+    **A per-rule `excluded:` key does NOT work for a stock rule, and swiftlint only WARNS about it.** Measured over one force unwrap in `Sources/` and the same in `Tests/`, with `force_unwrapping: {excluded: ".*/Tests/.*"}`: swiftlint reported BOTH files, exit 0, and wrote `warning: Configuration for 'force_unwrapping' rule contains the invalid key(s) 'excluded'.` So the test-target split cannot live in the configuration. It has to be the script's own partition.
+
+    **Airbnb's own swiftlint.yml does NOT name the three force rules.** Fetched from master. Their `only_rules` names `fatal_error_message`, `implicitly_unwrapped_optional`, the three legacy rules, `legacy_constant`, `unused_optional_binding`, `unowned_variable_capture`, `superfluous_disable_command`, `invalid_swiftlint_command`, `custom_rules`. The force rules are handled on the swiftformat side by `noForceUnwrapInTests` / `noForceTryInTests`, which is the polarity the card names. The three custom regex rules were copied verbatim from that file.
+
+    **The three custom rules work, and `match_kinds` does the scoping the card claims.** Measured over one probe file: `print`, `debugPrint`, `dump` and `Swift.print` each report `no_direct_standard_out_logs`; `#file` reports `no_file_literal`; `@unchecked Sendable` reports `no_unchecked_sendable`. The string literal `"print(this is a string, not a call)"` and the comment `// print(this is a comment)` each report NOTHING — `match_kinds: [identifier]` is what does that. `rule_id` in the JSON report is the custom rule's own key.
+
+    **The annotation escape hatch works.** The same `@unchecked Sendable` class under `// swiftlint:disable:next no_unchecked_sendable  the value is immutable` reported nothing, while the class without the comment reported.
+
+    **swiftlint reports the SYMLINK-RESOLVED absolute path in `.file`.** Measured: `cd "$(dirname "$f")" && pwd -P` plus the basename reproduces it exactly, through a `./` prefix and through a symlinked working directory. That is what lets the test-file partition be an exact string match rather than a regex.
+
+    **`swift package describe` gives the authoritative test target paths and costs 0.19-0.36 s.** It reports a custom `path:` target (`Custom/OddTests`) that no convention would find, it does NOT resolve dependencies (measured: exit 0 beside a dependency at `https://example.invalid/nope.git`), and `swift package --scratch-path <tmp> describe` keeps the `.build` directory out of the workspace.

+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m0n0j6kw3s2tasj32d23g2b1
+  text: |-
+    Implementation landed as `disallowed-constructs-swift`, a `files`-scope tool rule in `code-hygiene`.
+
+    **Design decisions, and what each was measured against.**
+
+    The rule runs ONE swiftlint invocation over every path it is given, with a child config that states `only_rules` (nine stock names plus `custom_rules`) and every option of every rule. It reuses the whole parent/child, status-gate and three-stderr-reading skeleton of `magic-numbers-swift`, `missing-docs-swift` and `function-length-swift`, so the shipped swiftlint rules are now four and share one shape.
+
+    **The test-target polarity split is the script's own partition, because it cannot be anything else.** swiftlint has no per-rule path filter for a stock rule and it does not refuse the key: measured, `excluded:` under `force_unwrapping:` is answered with a WARNING and both files still report. So the script builds a list of test-file paths and the `jq` filter drops a `force_unwrapping`, `force_try` or `force_cast` finding whose `file` is in that list. Two facts feed the list, as a UNION:
+
+    - the `Tests/` convention — a path whose first component is `Tests`, or which holds a `Tests` component anywhere;
+    - the test targets `swift package describe --type json` names, when the workspace root holds a `Package.swift`.
+
+    The manifest read is GUARDED, never required: `[ -f Package.swift ]` stands first, `2>/dev/null` swallows a manifest the tool cannot read, and a nonzero status leaves the convention standing alone — so `swift` is absent from `check_command` and a machine without it keeps the whole gate. Measured with `swift` off the PATH: `Tests/ProbeTests` keeps the carve-out and `Custom/OddTests` loses it. `swift package --scratch-path <tmp> describe` keeps `.build` out of the workspace; measured, the probe package holds no `.build` after the run.
+
+    The partition compares WHOLE resolved absolute paths rather than a regex, because a directory name holding a regex metacharacter would silently stop matching.
+
+    **A dead end worth recording.** The first probe for the manifest test staged `Package.swift` naming three targets and a file for only two of them. SPM refuses to describe such a package — `error: Source files for target ProbeTests should be located under 'Tests/ProbeTests'` at exit 1 — so the run fell back to the convention and the test failed for the right reason. The probe now stages a file under `Tests/ProbeTests` as well, and the test doc records the trap.
+
+    **Findings the card's table did not match, corrected against the rule files.**
+
+    - `unused_optional_binding` decides NO shipped prompt bullet. `builtin/validators/swift/rules/optionals.md` holds four bullets — force unwrap, `guard let` early exit, IUO, and no `Optional` where a default fits — and none of them is "check for nil, do not bind an unused value". The rule body puts `unused_optional_binding` in the "no shipped prompt rule asks" group. The gate therefore decides FIVE bullets across three prompt rules, not six.
+    - `optionals.md`'s IUO bullet sanctions two exceptions, `@IBOutlet` and "test fixtures set in `setUp()`". `mode: all_except_iboutlets` expresses the first; measured, no swiftlint option expresses the second, and `swiftlint rules implicitly_unwrapped_optional` names only `severity` and `mode`. `error-handling.md`'s `try!` bullet has the same shape, and `swiftlint rules force_try` names only `severity`. Both gaps are documented in the rule body under "Two prompt carve-outs no option expresses", with the directive as the recourse, and card ^c8fj21y was created to decide whether `implicitly_unwrapped_optional` should join the test-target partition.
+
+    **`supersedes` is empty**, per the card. `builtin/validators/README.md` said only two shipped tool rules declare no `supersedes`; that sentence was already stale for `idioms-swift` and is now corrected to name all four, with the reason the two Swift rules leave it empty stated separately from the reason the other two do.
+
+    **A gap in the sibling card's work, closed here.** `CODE_HYGIENE_IDIOMS_TOOL_RULES` was added to `expected_rules` and to the length sum of `test_code_hygiene_loads_its_rule_roster_and_the_callers_probe`, and NOT to `expected_supersedes` — the chain that actually asserts `supersedes.names()`. So nothing held `idioms-swift` to superseding nothing. Both idioms and disallowed-constructs are now in that chain.
+
+    **Counts re-measured over `builtin/validators/*/rules/*.md`**, not derived by arithmetic: 27 rules carry a `run` script, 16 state `scope: files`, 11 state `scope: workspace`, 24 call `mktemp`. Of the 16 files-scope scripts, 4 write the zero-argument guard on the first line and 12 write it under `set -e` alone.
